newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican debt relief scheme to miss target - CNBV.
newsitem.headline: Mexican debt relief scheme to miss target - CNBV.

text.p: The government is almost certain to miss its target for restructuring 2.1 million bank credits under a debt relief scheme known as the ADE, a top banking commission official said on Wednesday.

"There were 2.1 million restructurings that we had hoped for and we have completed more or less 1.098 million up to (the end of) August," Javier Gavito, vice-president of the National Banking and Securities Commission, told a news conference. "I don't think we'll get to two million."

He said the reasons the government would fail to meet its goals for the scheme, which cuts payments and extends maturities for debt-strapped Mexicans and aims to ease the level of bad loans in the ailing banking sector, were twofold.

"There were people who got out, who paid and didn't restructure; and there were others who were considered unrecoverable or not viable...they wouldn't have been able to make it even with a restructuring."
Mexican debtors were hit last year by sky-rocketing interest rates during the country's worst recession in 50 years and unpaid debts drove the banks to the brink of crisis.
